summary: Intermittent TLS 1.3 key_share truncation during large model shard downloads across peered VPCs causing gRPC stream stalls
description: Issue summary: Customers report intermittent failures pulling large model shards (50-250MB ranges) from Redwood artifact store when their private deployment uses VPC peering and corporate egress proxies. Failures present as gRPC stream stalls followed by TLS handshake errors (TLS 1.3 alert) during the handshake resume/early_data stage.
impact: Multiple production inference nodes in Nimbus AI's dedicated cluster intermittently fail to fetch model shards during rollout and autoscale events. Result is increased 5xx rate in their inference path and degraded throughput for latency-sensitive endpoints. Customer reports 8-12% failed shard fetch rate during peak traffic windows, triggering automated rollback attempts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private Redwood agent in Nimbus AI account (peered VPC to Redwood control VPC). 2) Scale serving pool to trigger concurrent model-shard fetches (50+ simultaneous range requests). 3) Observe gRPC streaming behavior and TLS logs on both agent and egress proxy. 4) Recreate with tcpdump on egress/peer path to capture TLS handshake fragments.
observed_behavior: gRPC streaming stalls mid-download (~10-40s in), followed by peer TLS handshake failures. Server logs show 'tls: unexpected message' and client logs indicate 'handshake failure, key_share mismatch' for TLS 1.3. Retries eventually succeed after backoff, but cause request timeouts and application-level retries.
expected_behavior: Large shard downloads should complete over a single persistent gRPC/TLS session without mid-stream handshake truncation. Retries should be minimal and not correlate with concurrent scale events.
hypothesis: During concurrent large-range downloads, an intermediate egress device (corporate proxy or NAT) is splitting TCP segments and reassembling in a way that truncates TLS 1.3 key_share extension in ClientHello or ServerHello when session resumption / early_data is used. Asymmetric return path via peering causes the reassembly to be inconsistent, producing malformed handshake on receiver and triggering TLS alerts.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial report received from Nimbus AI support engineer with client-side TLS logs and tcpdump snippets. Noted key_share alert entries in client debug logs.

2026-03-11: Reproduced in test account by triggering 60 concurrent shard fetches. Captured PCAPs on agent and egress appliance. Observed ClientHello split across two packets; second packet sometimes lost on return path due to an ECMP rebalancing event at the peering border.
2026-03-11: Correlated failing flows with spike in conntrack churn on customer's NAT appliance. Conntrack timeouts and ephemeral port reuse coincide with mid-download stalls.
2026-03-12: SRE ran targeted experiment disabling TLS 1.3 0-RTT/resumption on a canary agent; failure rate dropped to <1%. Indicates resumption/early_data interaction is a factor.

2026-03-12: Packet-level diffs show ClientHello key_share extension bytes present on origin but fragmented differently on the responder path. Suspect path MTU/segmentation or middlebox reassembly bug coupled with asymmetric peering routes.

2026-03-13: Eng validated that server-side (artifact store) accepts resumed sessions correctly; reproduced failure only when peered path included third-party egress proxy doing HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation for concurrent range requests.
Logs/Artifacts: PCAP IDs: nimbus-pcap-3372, redwood-agent-pcap-1089. Client TLS debug excerpt included in attachments.
Related: SUP-331900 (dns-answer-oscillation) investigated earlier for same customer's peering flaps during scale events.
Workaround tried: Enforcing single-threaded shard fetch reduced occurrence but is not viable for production throughput.

Next steps: Engage customer network team to inspect egress proxy behavior; propose disabling TLS 1.3 early_data on agent as short-term mitigation; plan server-side rejection of 0-RTT for peered flows as a safety policy.

resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: Instructed customer to disable TLS 1.3 early_data/session resumption on agent side for prod serving pool (config flag: agent.tls.disable_0rtt=true). This reduced failures to acceptable thresholds during peak. Long-term: Networking team will work with customer to (1) mitigate asymmetric ECMP rebalancing during shard fetch bursts, (2) update recommended runbook to avoid HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation on peered egress for range-preserved streams, and (3) implement server-side policy to reject 0-RTT for connections across known peered paths where middlebox interaction is present. Follow-up action:ENG-12488 to add detection/metrics for handshake-fragmentation anomalies and ENG-12489 to add server-side 0-RTT safety flag configurable per-customer.
